Your style

Comfortable, expressive, and pickier than you used to be.

You have quite a varied wardrobe: flowy dresses, tailored vests, shirts, well-fitted trousers, graphic T-shirts and kurta sets. You enjoy prints and saturated colours, but also have plenty of neutrals to ground them.

You seem to know exactly what makes you feel good in Indian clothing. Now, you're exploring how to bring that same confidence into tops and trousers, skirts and dresses.

What we noticed

What makes you feel good

You enjoy silhouettes that give you some structure while still leaving room to move: pieces that accentuate your shoulders and arms while keeping the rest of the silhouette forgiving, especially an A-line shape. That balance seems to be an important part of what makes you feel comfortable and confident.

You also feel especially good in clothes that give you height and length, like kurtis, palazzos and sarees.

What you're figuring out
  1. 01

    Tops + bottoms

    You want the same confidence in a contemporary wardrobe that you already have in Indian silhouettes.

  2. 02

    Proportion

    Particularly bottoms and midi lengths, and culottes without the sizing and proportion issues you've run into before.

  3. 03

    Fitted clothing

    Wanting to wear fitted pieces without losing the comfort your A-lines give you.

  4. 04

    Layering

    Harder in the heat, where most layering ideas assume weather you don't have.

Where we come in

Where we can help

01

Custom design

If you know the kind of silhouette you want but can't find the right version of it, or your proportions are specific enough that an existing cut just doesn't sit right, this is where we build it. Your preferences around shape, proportion, colour and comfort become part of the design.

02

Styling

Your Indian wardrobe already shows what works for you: structure at the shoulder, an A-line's forgiveness through the body, length that elongates. The work here is carrying that into the rest of your wardrobe.

Let's take these one at a time.

Proportion, decoded

One at a time · 02

Fixing culottes for good

When ready-made won't do it

The length has likely been the sticking point so far. We can measure you against your waist-to-hip ratio, hem width and length to get you the crop you actually have in mind.

What to wear on top

A top that's fitted or tucked at the waist, with a vertical line down the front. It's what balances the volume, so the look doesn't double up top and bottom. A flared peplum top or vertical stripes work the same way, bringing back the illusion of length.

One at a time · 03

Layering that survives the heat

In Chennai's humidity, layering rarely feels worth the effort. Done right, it's one of the simplest ways to make an outfit look and feel elevated.

Swipe for the next look

One at a time · 04

Fitted, without the discomfort

Swipe a piece to enlarge

None of these actually fit tight anywhere. The waist holds its shape through a gather or a twist in the fabric rather than a tailored cut, so the rest of the dress is free to move. Up top, the neckline (a halter, a drape, one shoulder) carries its own shape too. Satin, crepe and other fabrics with real weight and drape help here: they skim over the body instead of clinging to it.

The finishing touches

Bringing the spunk back

It doesn't have to mean statement pieces. Layered together, a few colourful, interesting pieces do just as much.
